name: Monport GT 30W Fiber
tagline: Split fiber laser engraver with autofocus from Monport
tldr: Monport GT 30W brings split-cabinet fiber marking with autofocus: useful for varying part heights. Strong alternative to Gweike G6 in the same class.
mainObjective: Entry fiber marking on small metal parts

priceRange.note: Official Monport store, Oct 2026: $2,440 to $2,690 depending on bundle

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

pros: Lowest price in the GT line at $2,440, with autofocus and electric lift (Monport store, Oct 2026)
Best beam quality figure Monport lists in the GT range (M² below 1.5), good for small text and QR codes
Same 550 mm maximum Z height and rotary support as the more powerful GT models
cons: No colour marking: Q-switched source with a fixed 80–120 ns pulse
0.75 mJ pulse energy and 0.08 mm listed marking depth: slow for deep engraving and thin-metal cut-outs
Smallest field in the line, 150 × 150 mm

faq.question: How deep and how fast does the Monport GT 30W mark metal?
faq.answer: Monport lists a maximum marking depth of 0.08 mm and a top galvo speed of 10,000 mm/s for the GT 30W; deeper engraving comes from repeated passes. In our benchmark, a filled 10 × 10 cm logo on stainless steel takes about 4–11 minutes depending on fill density.

faq.question: Does the GT 30W do colour marking on stainless steel?
faq.answer: Not in a controlled way. It uses a Q-switched source with a fixed 80–120 ns pulse and a 30–60 kHz frequency range. Monport lists colour engraving only for the MOPA models of the GT series, which adjust pulse width from 2 to 500 ns.

faq.question: GT 30W or GT 50W: which one should I buy?
faq.answer: The GT 30W costs $2,440 on Monport's store (October 2026), about $1,100 less than the GT 50W. It suits tags, tools and tumblers on a 150 × 150 mm field. The GT 50W adds pulse energy (1.25 mJ vs 0.75 mJ), a 200 × 200 mm field and slightly more depth (0.10 mm listed), which helps for deeper logos and thin-metal cut-outs.

standoutFeatures.title: Autofocus at the lowest GT price
standoutFeatures.body: At $2,440 the GT 30W keeps the series features: autofocus, electric lift, 550 mm maximum Z height and rotary support. Only the source and the field size change.

standoutFeatures.title: Tight beam for fine detail
standoutFeatures.body: Monport lists M² below 1.5 for the GT 30W, against below 1.8 for the other GT models. For small serial numbers, QR codes and jewelry text, the lower power is not a handicap.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 30W SKU on Monport GT Fiber. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Fix parts firmly; start with low power test squares on scrap metal. Rotary adds complexity: budget time to learn indexing.
primaryUse: Desktop fiber marking for jewelry-scale and test jobs

images.alt: Monport GT 30W Fiber laser engraver: Monport

editorialDepth.advantages: Monport GT Fiber 30W fits shops that mark stainless, aluminum, and tools daily without a CO₂ bay. A solid bench option for jewelry, tags, and small batches.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if wood, leather, or cast acrylic pay your bills. Deep metal cutting and large industrial panels often need more fiber headroom (50W, 60W or 100W) or a different machine class.
